title: Partner pipeline tradeoffs + playbook sync
summary: Align on co-sell account prioritization, decide pilot scope and hosting model for Cobalt Health, surface security gating items, agree next steps and who will own pilot pricing and benchmark runs.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
pilot scope, success metrics and pricing guardrails
integration touchpoints for partner co-sell ops
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-03 | 09:00 PT | Duration ~72m | Notes/Recap at end
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena, Tom, Priya, Scott (Cobalt + channel).

[00:00] Maya: ok good morning everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — prioritize the joint accounts, decide pilot hosting model, and surface any security blockers.
[00:37] Lena: thanks Maya, yea we're trying to move three pilot accounts into a Q4 exec review, biggest ask from sales is predictable latency and contractual data residency.
[01:12] Tom: if we can promise <150ms tail latency for summary flows that's a huge win; otherwise risk is they go with incumbent.
[01:45] Daniel: just to set expectations, latency depends a lot on model variant and routing. hosted can hit low latencies but dedicated gives predictable throughput. private (VPC) is the most complex — more hook ups for KMS and network but meets residency.
[02:20] Priya: from compliance we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SSO via SAML, and confirmation on key management — customer-managed KMS ideally. also SOC 2 type II attestation copy.
[02:52] Maya: noted. we have a security pack; we'll share SOC2, architecture diagram, and an integration checklist after this. link: https://redwood.docs/partner-security-pack-09-03 (shared).
[03:20] Scott: question — will Redwood support co-sell revenue splits or deal registration? just want to be clear on enablement.
[03:42] Maya: deal registration yes, co-sell economics are handled through our channel team; we'll loop in ops after this call.
[04:10] Lena: ok on pilot scope, we want 1) clinical note summarization (P1) and 2) QM scoring for intake forms (P2). P1 needs low latency, P2 is throughput-heavy but can be batch.
[04:50] Daniel: that's helpful — for P1 we suggest a mid-size LLM with KV cache priming and low-latency routing; for P2 we can recommend quantized model + batching to reduce unit cost.
[05:25] Tom: cost is a big gating factor. our finance echos that any pilot that ramps >$10k/month needs exec sign-off.
[05:58] Maya: on pricing we've done a pilot guardrail model: usage cap + committed reserved capacity if they want predictable pricing. we'll provide sample numbers in the pilot deck.
[06:32] Priya: on data retention — logs kept for 30 days by default, can be extended but needs contract change. can we get an initial SLA for log retention?
[07:00] Daniel: default retention 30d, we can support longer retention in Dedicated or Private, but storage cost increases.
[07:35] Lena: how does automatic fallback work? if dedicated pool is saturated, will requests go to hosted and lose residency?
[08:05] Daniel: good point — fallback policies are configurable. for regulated workloads we disable cross-region fallback; instead we queue or throttle. otherwise fallback to a compatible model variant in same legal boundary is possible.
[08:42] Maya: tradeoff conversation — you can get lower cost with autoscaling+fallback but lose strict residency guarantees. the partner ask is: are we willing to take some risk for cost?
[09:18] Tom: sales preference is guaranteed residency for health clients, cost is secondary but still constrained.
[09:45] Priya: security gating: SSO, KMS, audit logs, pen test window, and contractual indemnity language — we will send a short RACI of legal requirements.
[10:12] Maya: thanks. we'll assign a SOW owner and a security point of contact.
[10:40] Scott: for partner ops, what's the handoff cadence? we usually prefer weekly syncs until pilot is launched.
[11:05] Maya: weekly for initial 6 weeks, then biweekly. we'll also add a shared spreadsheet for account status. link: https://sheets.redwood/partner-pipeline-cobalt (shared).
[11:40] Daniel: technical deep-dive — quick note on KV cache and model selection: if clinical notes are highly repetitive, prefix caching will notably reduce tokens and latency. but if notes vary, caching helps less.
[12:15] Lena: yes notes are semi-structured with templated headings, caching could help. do we support custom tokenizers for clinical shorthand?
[12:46] Daniel: we can add preprocessing on the request path; tokenizer customization is medium complexity but doable for pilot.
[13:20] Tom: any competitor we should be mindful of on these accounts? we've heard from BigCloudAI and EdgeServe. BigCloudAI pitches integrated analytics, EdgeServe pitches on-prem simplicity.
[13:55] Maya: noted — we'll prepare a competitive header for the AE brief.
[14:20] Priya: about encryption at rest — on hosted we use provider-managed keys by default; on private/dedicated we can use customer-managed KMS (HSM integration possible).
[14:50] Daniel: HSM brings procurement overhead; allow 3-6 weeks for key provisioning with some cloud providers.
[15:20] Lena: timeline — customer wants a pilot in the next 6-8 weeks. is that realistic?
[15:45] Maya: with a focused scope (P1 only) and using hosted or dedicated it's doable in ~6 weeks. private adds 4-6 weeks.
[16:10] Tom: ok let's keep P1 as the initial pilot for timeline reasons.
[16:35] Daniel: action: we'll produce an architecture diagram for hosted vs dedicated vs private mapping to the pilot features.
[17:00] Maya: and we'll provide pricing scenarios and a short SOW template.
[17:25] Priya: we'll send the compliance matrix and list of mandatory clauses by end of week.
[17:50] Scott: partner team will prepare a co-sell win plan and intro deck for the three prioritized accounts.
[18:20] Maya: quick callouts — latency target <150ms p95 for P1, success metric = accuracy of summarization on our eval set + user acceptance test, budget guardrail $10k/month for pilot.
[18:55] Lena: can we run a small benchmark with a redwood-hosted model on a 1k-sample set? we can share sample data (PHI redacted) under NDA.
[19:25] Daniel: yes, we can do an offline benchmark first; we'll need a sanitized dataset and a short prompt template.
[19:50] Tom: logistics — who sends the NDA and who's the legal contact?
[20:12] Maya: I'll send the NDA + pilot SOW draft later today. legal contact is me for initial review.
[20:40] Priya: can we confirm who will own run-of-bench results and whether Redwood will share model debug logs?
[21:05] Daniel: we'll share aggregate metrics and per-prompt traces but not raw token-level logs unless agreed in contract.
[21:40] Scott: for partner ops, we'll register these leads in our CRM and create a joint opportunity.
[22:05] Maya: final recap coming up. any outstanding blockers?
[22:30] Lena: security sign-off timeline — we need an SLA on remediation windows for critical vulnerabilities.
[22:55] Priya: yes, and a commitment to periodic pen test windows and evidence of fixes.
[23:20] Daniel: we can commit to TTR (time to respond) SLAs in the enterprise addendum.
[23:45] Maya: great. recap + next steps coming in email.
[24:05] (audio wraps, a few people drop off and rejoin, some crosstalk).

End of transcript — detailed action items and next steps below.

Partners to set up weekly ops cadence and register opportunities in CRM (Scott) - weekly starting 2026-09-07
